title: Build cache in the registry; pull requests from collaborators only
author: anton-matosov
body:
CI rebuilt every image from scratch on every run. Each image now keeps a build cache per architecture in its own GHCR package, as `cache-amd64` / `cache-arm64` tags, read and written by every CI run. Local builds don't use it.

The repository takes no outside contributions, so forks are out of scope for every feature: the fork conditions in the images workflow are gone, and the cache needs no fork fallback. Both decisions are recorded as ADRs 0020 and 0021.

## Results

| Run | Build step (amd64 / arm64) | Steps from cache (amd64 / arm64) |
|---|---|---|
| `main`, no cache (3 recent runs) | ~2m15s / ~2m | none |
| This PR, first run (fills the cache) | 1m51s / 2m13s | 0 / 0 |
| This PR, second run | **45s / 40s** | **58 / 60** |

The first run logs `failed to configure registry cache importer: …: not found` for each image: the cache did not exist yet. It is harmless and the run passed. The whole job still takes about 3 minutes, mostly smoke tests, which the cache does not affect.

## Test plan
- [x] `bake --print` shows no cache without `CACHE`, and the right `:cache-<arch>` refs for all four images with it
- [x] `.github/scripts/images.sh` still lists the images parent first
- [x] actionlint passes
- [x] The first run created `cache-amd64` and `cache-arm64` on all four packages
- [x] The second run served nearly every step from the cache, building in about a third of the time
